items.title: Talent Acquisition Specialist , GTM & Corporate - EMEA
items.description: ABOUT MISTRAL Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. THE ROLE As a member of the EMEA Talent Acquisition team focused on Corporate and Go-To-Market hiring, you will be instrumental in building and scaling Mistral's EMEA-based teams across both corporate functions and revenue-generating roles. Joining early means you'll help shape our recruitment strategy and operations, partnering closely with leaders across Corporate functions (Finance, Legal, People, Operations, Marketing, Communications) and GTM functions (Sales, Pre-Sales/Solutions, Partnerships, Customer Success, and Revenue Operations). Your work will directly influence Mistral's commercial and operational success by ensuring we find and engage exceptional operators who will drive Mistral's growth across the EMEA region. In this role, you'll also foster a strong candidate experience and help establish recruiting best practices as we expand across multiple EMEA markets. WHAT YOU WILL DO STAKEHOLDER PARTNERSHIP - Partner deeply with Corporate and GTM leaders — from CRO and VP Sales to Finance, Legal, and People leadership — to understand hiring needs, define role specs, and identify the right talent across multiple EMEA markets. - Own full-cycle recruitment across Corporate and GTM functions: Sales, Finance, Legal, People/HR, Marketing, and Communications roles. - Advise hiring managers on market mapping, leveling, comp positioning, and the competitive landscape for EMEA talent, accounting for local market nuances, benchmarking, and statutory differences across countries. - Translate the nuances of each role into compelling, accurate, and locally relevant candidate outreach. END-TO-END RECRUITMENT - Own the full recruiting lifecycle from sourcing to close, operating with autonomy on complex, high-volume roles across Corporate and GTM. - Source passive and active candidates across EMEA talent pools, particularly in AI/ML, open-source software, enterprise infrastructure, and regional corporate markets. - Conduct intake and calibration sessions with hiring managers to align on ideal candidate profiles and stage expectations. - Drive efficient, high-conversion pipelines and close candidates in a fiercely competitive market for senior talent across multiple geographies and languages. - Navigate cross-border hiring complexity, including relocation, remote-friendly offers, and country-specific employment frameworks. CANDIDATE EXPERIENCE & SELLING MISTRAL - Guide candidates through the hiring process with clear communication and a compelling narrative about Mistral's mission, culture, and trajectory. - Articulate Mistral's positioning in the AI landscape — frontier models, open-weight philosophy, and enterprise credibility — to differentiate us against better-known competitors. - Provide candidates with real insight into our GTM motion, corporate operations, growth plans, and the specific impact of their role. - Deliver a high-quality, respectful candidate experience at every stage, regardless of outcome. RECRUITING OPERATIONS & DATA-DRIVEN IMPROVEMENT - Develop and refine recruiting processes, tools, and documentation to improve outcomes and efficiency. - Use data to diagnose pipeline issues (e.g., drop-off at specific stages, time-to-fill by role, offer acceptance rates) and propose targeted solutions. - Build and maintain market maps, competitive intel, and talent pools for key EMEA Corporate and GTM segments. - Standardize interview rubrics, scorecards, and debrief practices across EMEA hiring teams, while respecting local market and language differences. RAISING THE BAR - Collaborate with Corporate and GTM leadership and the broader Talent team to continuously elevate our hiring standards. - Contribute to defining and evolving our EMEA talent acquisition strategy as we scale from early team to a mature, multi-region organization. - Partner on employer-brand and outbound sourcing initiatives that position Mistral as a destination for top Corporate and GTM talent in EMEA. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - 6+ years of recruiting experience, including 2+ years in a startup or high-growth B2B SaaS/infrastructure company, with a focus on Corporate functions and/or Sales/GTM roles. - Demonstrated ability to independently hire across the full GTM stack — from Enterprise AE’s to GTM leadership — as well as key Corporate functions (Finance, Legal, People, Marketing, Operations). - Deep network and sourcing expertise in EMEA talent markets, particularly in AI/ML, open-source, developer tools, or enterprise software. - Track record of hiring in competitive, candidate-scarce markets where candidates have multiple offers, including cross-border and multi-language hiring. - Experience working across multiple EMEA markets and comfort with country-specific comp, benefits, and employment nuance. - Willingness to work on other roles as needs come up. - Comfort navigating ambiguity and switching between strategic planning and hands-on execution. - Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence peers and senior stakeholders without direct authority. - Organized, detail-oriented, and able to juggle shifting priorities across a high-volume hiring slate spanning two function families. - Professional experience with modern recruiting tools such as Ashby. - Familiarity with the AI/ML landscape and the ability to credibly discuss frontier model capabilities with technical GTM and corporate candidates. WHAT WE OFFER We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks. For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page https://app.notion.com/p/mistralai/Benefits-at-Mistral-36e6ba59a7fe836b93dd01737fcc27ef?source=copy_link. PRIVACY POLICY Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy https://legal.mistral.ai/terms/applicant-privacy-policy.

items.description: In 2026, we launched Computer, the defining product for the new era of agentic AI. We’ve scaled beyond the millions of people using Perplexity every day for research, shopping, investing and curiosity into a new paradigm of using AI to transform knowledge into action. Product Managers at Perplexity work closely with design and engineering, focusing on the core agentic and search experiences. The ideal candidate should have strong communication and writing skills, the ability to envision innovative technology, and willingness to reimagine work to be more efficient and creative. Ideal candidates have a passion in a particular industry that they are domain experts in: in the application please highlight which industry you are most interested in innovating. THE ROLE The Core Experience team owns the foundational interactions that define how people use Perplexity every day. This includes how users begin and continue work, understand what the product is doing, navigate and find what they need, manage their context and preferences, collaborate with others, and return to ongoing work across platforms. You will identify the highest-leverage user problems, translate them into clear product direction, and partner closely with design, engineering, data science, and research to deliver experiences that feel fast, intuitive, cohesive, and dependable. This role requires strong product judgment, deep user empathy, analytical rigor, and an exceptional eye for detail. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Anticipate opportunities for innovation and value in enterprise industries. - Envision new experiences and deliver a long-term vision. - Understanding of levers for product-led growth and retention. - Work closely with engineering and design to align product expectations and capabilities. - Work with research to evaluate and steer nondeterministic models into the high value outcomes for users. - Have conviction to make difficult product decisions in the face of uncertainty. - Develop a deep understanding of user needs, behaviors, and friction through direct product use, qualitative research, product data, and experimentation. - Make complex AI behavior understandable and controllable through clear interaction models, thoughtful defaults, and well-designed feedback. - Drive alignment when improvements span multiple product surfaces, platforms, or teams. - Communicate product decisions, tradeoffs, progress, and learnings clearly to leadership and cross-functional partners. QUALIFICATIONS - Strong experience with product management and leadership. - Strong experience working with data and metrics. - Experience with productivity and knowledge work products. - Experience with prototyping and data visualization. - Experience with building data driven flywheels for iterative improvement. - Thrives in a small, agile team: has initiative and desire for ownership. - 4+ years of product management experience. OUR MISSION Perplexity's mission is to power curiosity. Curious people are the people who drive change in the world. Driving change is a continuous cycle of learning, building, and integrating. Learn: curious people constantly learn new things by asking more. They question the status quo in their own expertise and they constantly learn outside of it. Research is essential to them and never ending. Build: curious people make and create things, to show the world their new answers to problems no one else ever questioned. They take action on what they've learned. Makers need tools to create their products, their companies, their reality. Integrate: they must interact with the world as it is to drive change and adoption. True leaders do not simply build something and hope. They must have armies of agents and workers who can constantly work in millions of small ways. Repeat. For curious people this is a cycle that never ends.

items.title: Global Public Policy Manager, Compute, Infrastructure & Sovereign AI
items.description: WHO ARE WE? Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems. We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that. We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us! ABOUT THE ROLE Cohere is seeking a Global Public Policy Manager to lead policy engagement on compute infrastructure, export controls, AI competitiveness, and sovereign AI strategies. Governments increasingly view AI as critical national infrastructure and are investing heavily in compute capacity, energy resources, and domestic AI ecosystems. This role will help position Cohere as a trusted partner in emerging discussions around AI infrastructure, national competitiveness, and sovereign AI deployment. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES - Monitor and analyze developments related to AI infrastructure, data centers, energy policy, semiconductor policy, export controls, and national AI strategies. - Develop policy positions on sovereign AI, compute access, digital sovereignty, and AI competitiveness. - Support engagement with governments developing AI infrastructure investment programs and national AI initiatives. - Collaborate with commercial, product, and corporate development teams on strategic opportunities involving public-private partnerships. - Represent Cohere in policy discussions related to AI infrastructure, energy requirements, and technology competitiveness. - Produce policy analysis and thought leadership on AI infrastructure and sovereign AI trends. QUALIFICATIONS - 5–7 years of experience in public policy, technology policy, trade policy, energy policy, national security policy, or related fields. - Strong understanding of geopolitical technology issues, AI infrastructure, export controls, or digital sovereignty. - Ability to assess emerging policy developments and identify strategic business implications. - Excellent analytical and stakeholder engagement skills. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS - Experience working on semiconductors, cloud infrastructure, energy policy, telecommunications, or national competitiveness issues. - Familiarity with government AI investment programs and international technology policy. FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS: - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch. - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health. - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme. - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent. - Annual enrichment benefits: Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit. Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching. - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!) - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite. HOW AND WHERE WE WORK: - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon. - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events. - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city. - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly. If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12a6IrLdF3kI2nonKSr4tiFuz18rLQbaeYV-JM9L4o9Q/edit, and we will work together to meet your needs. We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider. Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers https://cohere.com/careers page.

items.description: We're looking for a Growth Brand Designer to sit at the intersection of brand craft and growth performance. You'll be the designer who makes Perplexity's highest-volume, highest-leverage marketing surfaces — paid ads, social, lifecycle email, and campaign assets — look unmistakably Perplexity while actually moving the numbers. This is a shipping role, but it's equally a thinking role. Strategic concepting is a big part of the job: you'll sit with the Growth team as an ideator — generating campaign concepts, testing hypotheses, and shaping the creative strategy behind the work — not just executing briefs handed to you. The ideas you bring to the table matter as much as the assets you ship. You'll produce a steady stream of ad and campaign creative across formats and channels, then work with Growth to read the results and iterate. You care about conversion and craft in equal measure: you'd never ship an off-brand asset to win a test, and you'd never hide behind polish when the data says a concept isn't working. You'll report into the Brand/Creative Studio team and work closely with Growth, Product Marketing, Brand, and our motion and web designers. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Drive strategic concepting for growth campaigns — bring original ideas, angles, and creative territories to the table, and shape the brief rather than just receiving it - Operate as a true ideation partner to the Growth team: co-develop campaign strategy, propose test hypotheses, and pitch concepts that open up new creative directions - Own the design of growth creative end-to-end — paid social and display ads, campaign assets, and lifecycle email — from concept to shipped asset - Design for volume and velocity: build variant sets, test hypotheses, and iterate on winners with the Growth team using real performance data - Partner with Brand to keep visual consistency across every growth touchpoint as our brand system evolves - Collaborate with our motion designer and web designer so campaigns feel cohesive from the first ad impression to the landing page - Bring a strong point of view on what makes performance creative great — and push back when a "best practice" would cheapen the brand WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - A strong portfolio of growth and brand design work — paid ads, social campaigns, lifecycle email, campaign systems — that shows both craft and results - Proven strategic concepting ability: you can show campaigns where the idea was yours, not just the execution, and articulate the thinking behind them - Excellent visual design skills with a clear sense of brand, typography, layout, and composition - Hands-on experience designing performance creative at a consumer or prosumer tech company, including working directly with growth or performance marketing teams - Fluency reading creative performance data (CTR, conversion, hook rates) and translating it into design decisions - Ability to work fast, manage a high volume of deliverables across channels, and iterate quickly without dropping the quality bar - Fluency in Figma and the Adobe Creative Suite - An instinct for building repeatable systems — templates, variant frameworks, asset kits — rather than one-off files - 5+ years of industry experience NICE TO HAVE - Motion design skills — animated ads, short-form video for social, or After Effects fluency - Familiarity with ad platform specs and constraints (Meta, Google, TikTok, X, YouTube) and how they shape creative decisions - Experience using AI-assisted design and image-generation workflows to scale creative output - Copywriting instincts — you can tighten a headline when there's no writer in the room

items.title: Member of Technical Staff (TPM, Inference)
items.description: Perplexity is looking for a technical program manager to be the connective tissue between our model providers, engineering, and product teams, driving our core inference platform forward. Perplexity runs one of the highest-throughput inference stacks in the industry, serving Ask, Computer, and API traffic across a large and constantly shifting portfolio of first-party and third-party models. This role sits at the intersection of product, engineering, and finance: you'll orchestrate across model providers and internal teams to keep new models and capacity moving smoothly into production, while executing the roadmap for the inference platform itself. The ideal candidate has strong technical judgment, thrives coordinating across teams and external partners with competing timelines, and is energized by building the operating model for a function that doesn't have much precedent yet. OUR MISSION Perplexity's mission is to power curiosity. Curious people are the people who drive change in the world. Driving change is a continuous cycle of learning, building, and integrating. Learn: curious people constantly learn new things by asking more. They question the status quo in their own expertise and they constantly learn outside of it. Research is essential to them and never ending. Build: curious people make and create things, to show the world their new answers to problems no one else ever questioned. They take action on what they've learned. Makers need tools to create their products, their companies, their reality. Integrate: they must interact with the world as it is to drive change and adoption. True leaders do not simply build something and hope. They must have armies of agents and workers who can constantly work in millions of small ways. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Execute the roadmap for the inference platform request handling, rate limits and quotas, usage controls, and the reliability and observability surface engineering and product teams depend on - Be the connective tissue between model providers and Perplexity's engineering and product teams coordinating onboarding, launch readiness, and rollout for new models and capacity - Drive latency, throughput, uptime, and cost-efficiency as core execution metrics, surfacing tradeoffs between them rather than letting them become side effects - Run the operating model for model-release and optimization programs, including day-zero launches, across performance engineering, infrastructure, and product teams - Lead cross-functional delivery for inference-stack changes, from planning through launch and post-launch validation - Build the mechanisms that make releases predictable rituals, dashboards, launch checklists so inference releases stay low-risk at Perplexity's scale - Partner with GPU capacity and compute teams to reconcile execution decisions against cost, capacity, and vendor constraints QUALIFICATIONS - Strong experience with technical program management or product management in infrastructure, distributed systems, or ML/model-serving products - Direct experience with production LLM or ML inference understanding what makes serving fast, reliable, and cheap rather than just what a roadmap slide says about it - Comfort orchestrating across external partners and internal engineering teams with competing priorities and timelines - Experience with data and metrics, and the judgment to surface difficult tradeoffs between latency, throughput, uptime, and cost - Thrives in a small, agile team; has initiative and desire for ownership without much precedent to lean on - 6+ years of combined technical program management or product management experience

items.title: Practicante administrativo
items.description: Funciones principales Apoyar la coordinación de los ingresos del personal operativo para cada turno de operación. Llevar el control de insumos, papelería y demás recursos necesarios para la operación. Brindar soporte administrativo a la Operation Manager y Team Managers Realizar seguimiento a las solicitudes administrativas relacionadas con Recursos Humanos y otras áreas de apoyo. Apoyar el proceso de ingreso de nuevos colaboradores, asegurando la actualización de las bases de datos y archivos del personal. Gestionar la entrega de dotación y registro de huella. Administrar el inventario de dotación, realizando el control de entradas, salidas y existencias. Organizar y actualizar el archivo físico y digital de la documentación del área de Operaciones. Recibir, registrar y realizar seguimiento a las incapacidades remitidas al correo del área, garantizando su correcto control y archivo. Realizar el Onboarding al personal que ingresa y Offboarding al personal que sale Ejecutar las demás funciones inherentes al cargo que le sean asignadas por el jefe inmediato, de acuerdo con las necesidades de la operación. Cualificaciones: Atención al detalle Organización Habilidades de comunicación Discreción y manejo de información confidencial Orientación al servicio interno y al trabajo en equipo

Apoyar la generación de informes periódicos para las áreas interesadas. Garantizar la calidad e integridad de la información utilizada en los análisis. Buena comunicación y organización. Capacidad de gestionar múltiples tareas y cumplir plazos.
